page: Amazon Web Services r6id.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with a dedicated Intel Xeon 8375C processor, delivering 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The processor includes a 54 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core.

For local storage, the r6id.16xlarge includes 3800 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, offering high-speed local read and write capabilities directly attached to the hypervisor. Networking is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps. There are no GPUs bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core CPU performance, particularly in passmark CPU tests, software compilation, and ray tracing. Database operations and static web serving throughput also rank in the top tier, while single-core performance and memory bandwidth remain in the average range. The hardware profile and benchmark results make this instance highly suitable for memory-intensive databases, large-scale data processing, software compilation pipelines, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.

The instance includes 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results show strong multi-core CPU performance, high database operation throughput, and efficient software compilation capabilities, while single-core metrics and memory bandwidth align with average tiers. This hardware configuration offers a balanced resource density for memory-heavy applications without the added cost of GPU acceleration. It is well-suited for hosting large databases, processing complex data pipelines, and executing multi-threaded enterprise workloads.
